==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|necessarye}}, from {{der|en|fro|necessaire}}, from {{der|en|la|necessārius||[[unavoidable]], [[inevitable]], [[require]]d}}, variant of {{m|la|necesse||[[unavoidable]], [[inevitable]]}}, probably from {{m|la|ne}} or {{m|la|non}} {{m|la|cessus|cessum}}, from the perfect passive participle of {{m|la|cēdō||[[yield]]; [[avoid]], [[withdraw]]}}; see [[cede]]. Older use as a noun in reference to an outhouse or lavatory under the influence of English and {{cog|la|necessārium}}, a medieval term for the place for monks’ “unavoidable” business, usually located behind or attached to monastic dormitories. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈnɛs.ə.sɹi/|/ˈnɛs.əˌsɛ.ɹi/|a=RP}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-necessary.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈnɛs.əˌsɛ.ɹi/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-necessary.ogg|a=US}} * {{lb|en|nonstandard}} {{IPA|en|/ˈnɛs.ə.ɹi/}} * {{IPA|en|/nᵻˈsɛsᵊ.ri/|a=North India}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈnɛs.ə.sə.ri/|a=South India}} * {{hyph|en|ne|ces|sar|y}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj|er,more}} # [[required|Required]], [[essential]], whether logically inescapable or [[needed]] in order to achieve a desired result or avoid some penalty. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:requisite}} #: {{ant|en|unnecessary}} #: {{ux|en|Although I wished to think that all was false, it was yet '''necessary''' that I, who thus thought, must in some sense exist.}} #: {{ux|en|It is absolutely '''necessary''' that you call and confirm your appointment.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Timon of Athens|III|vi|lines=1258-60|text=''[[first|1]].[[senator|Sen]].'' ...The [[fault]][['s|s]] Bloody:
'Tis [[necessary]] he should [[die|dye]]:
Nothing [[embolden|imboldens]] [[sin]]ne so much, as Mercy.}} # [[unavoidable|Unavoidable]], [[inevitable]]. #: {{syn|en|inevitable|natural}} #: {{ant|en|evitable|incidental|impossible}} #: {{ux|en|If it is absolutely '''necessary''' to use public computers, you should plan ahead and forward your e-mail to a temporary, disposable account.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Julius_Caesar|II|ii|lines=1020-25|text=''[[Caesar|Cæs]]''. Cowards [[die|dye]] many times before their deaths,
The valiant [[never|neuer]] taste of death but once:
Of all the Wonders that I yet [[have|haue]] heard,
It [[seems|seemes]] to me most strange that men should [[fear]]e,
Seeing that death, a [[necessary]] end
Will come, when it will come.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[determined|Determined]], [[involuntary]]: [[act]]ing from [[compulsion]] [[rather]] than [[free will]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1871|author=Richard Holt Hutton|title=Essays|volume=I|page=53 |passage=But that a '''necessary''' being should give birth to a being with any amount, however limited, of moral freedom, is infinitely less conceivable than that parents of the insect or fish type should give birth to a perfect mammal.}} ====Derived terms====
